risks: Concurrent agent runs push to this branch. Take the tip from `git ls-remote origin refs/heads/feature/agentic-enterprise-platform`, merge (never rebase, never force-push), revalidate, push. This run hit exactly that race: the remote had moved to 1c2377e by the time the commit was ready.

Two concurrent runs can claim the same task ID. Run 61 had already taken NEX-060 and NEX-061 for the policy-gate fix; this run's derive_assurance slice is NEX-062. Read the execution log before assigning an ID.

The acr negation veto is deliberately blunt: `mfa:not-sms` reads as single-factor because the function cannot tell 'multi-factor but not by SMS' from 'multi-factor not required' without a level registry. Understating refuses a step-up; overstating spends one that never happened. Accepted.
Numeric level conventions (aal2/loa3/ial2/urn:okta:loa:2) are deliberately unmapped and read as single-factor. Mapping them is a vocabulary change needing an ADR, not a patch.

`step-up` is enforced against the delegator's assurance at grant time. A delegation granted at single-factor stays single-factor even if the human later steps up - they must re-grant. Intentional (ADR-015), will surprise an operator.
The rate-limit obligation is a per-process bound with the in-memory adapter. A multi-replica deployment gets N per window per process until a shared-store adapter is wired.
Ten slices now stack in PR #5. Review cost is real.

decisions_this_run: D-062a: match acr by segment, not substring. `mfa-optional`, `mfa-not-required`, `mfa-disabled` and `not-multifactor` all name multi-factor in order to deny it; a substring match read every one as stepped up, so a login the IdP labelled as not stepped-up could spend a step-up obligation.

D-062b: let an adjacent negation veto a marker, and accept the blunt direction. `mfa:not-sms` reads as single-factor because distinguishing 'multi-factor but not SMS' from 'multi-factor not required' needs a level registry this build does not have. Understating refuses a step-up; overstating grants one that never happened.

D-062c: leave numeric level conventions unmapped and say so in the docstring. `ial2` is identity proofing, not a factor count, and `aal2` is reachable with one factor at some providers. Mapping them would guess at provider-specific semantics inside an enforcement path; it needs an ADR.

D-062d: put the end-to-end cases in the existing relying-party test file rather than the new one. That file already owns the signing helpers; duplicating them in the new module would have invented a second fixture style for one assertion.

D-062e: take NEX-062 rather than NEX-060/061. Run 61 had already used both for the policy-gate fix and left this slice as its 'next exact action'. Two runs writing the same ID would make the log ambiguous.
D-062f: merge the concurrent push rather than rebase. The remote had advanced to 1c2377e (docs-only) while this run was testing. Merging preserves both histories and is the only allowed resolution.
run_summary: The step-up control rested on `derive_assurance`, the OIDC acr/amr mapping, and that function had no direct test. Writing one found a live fail-open: it matched acr by substring, so `urn:acme:mfa-optional`, `mfa-not-required`, `mfa-disabled` and `not-multifactor` all resolved to multi-factor. In an enforcement path that is the difference between granting and refusing authority, and ADR-015 makes this one derived fact the basis of the step-up obligation. The fix matches acr by segment and lets an adjacent negation veto a marker; numeric level conventions stay deliberately unmapped with the reason written into the docstring. Twelve of the new cases fail against the previous implementation and pass against this one, so the regression is genuinely pinned rather than merely described. The commit and push survived a race with a concurrent run that had moved the remote tip; that was resolved by merging, never rebasing. Honest status: IMPLEMENTED, TESTED, COMMITTED, PUSHED - CI for this head has not been polled, so NEX-062 is not yet VERIFIED and is not listed as such.
